name: Walt Embry
languages: Army Tagalog (enough to order a beer and apologise)
equipment: Heavy overcoat, navy, ex-Army, with a torn lining where he keeps a spare key to everything
.38 revolver (Smith & Wesson Military & Police), 6 rounds loaded, in a shoulder holster that has worn a shiny patch on his shirt
Blackjack, leather, in the overcoat pocket
Fedora, grey, with a ferry ticket in the band
Notebook and two pencils, one always broken
Lock picks in a leather roll he is not licensed to carry
A roll of nickels for the payphone
Keys to the agency office, the agency safe, and a 1947 Ford coupe that will not start in the rain
His private investigator's licence and, in the same wallet, his old Port Calloway PD badge number on a card
features: Seen Worse (Ex-Service origin: advantage on saves against being frightened and against the Shaken condition; the first time each combat he is hit by a firearm, he keeps his reaction and any readied action)
Hunch (Private Eye: once per short or long rest, ask the GM one yes-or-no question about a lead he has personally encountered in this case and get a true answer)
Gumshoe (Private Eye: proficiency bonus doubled for Investigation and Insight checks)

Size Them Up (Private Eye, 2nd level: as a bonus action, study one creature within 60 ft; his next attack against it this turn has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 damage on a hit; twice per short rest, his WIS modifier)

Specialty: Shamus (Private Eye, 3rd level: Hunch can be used twice per short rest, and once per long rest he can ask 'who?' about a single event instead of a yes-or-no question, getting a name or 'nobody you've met')

Old Precinct (Ex-Cop background: he knows how the Port Calloway PD works from the inside, which desk sergeants take money and which cops still owe him; he can get a police record pulled for the price of a drink)

personality.traits: I talk slowly, listen fast, and write everything down in a notebook nobody else can read. I make terrible coffee and offer it to everyone. I am kind to old women, dogs and drunks, and rude to anyone in a good suit.
personality.ideals: Somebody ought to know what really happened. Even if nobody does anything about it, somebody ought to know.
personality.bonds: The agency. It is two rooms, three weeks behind on the rent and the only thing I have ever built. And the people in it, though I would rather be shot than say so.
personality.flaws: I left the force because I would not look away from something, and I have been telling myself that story for six years so that I do not have to remember the three other times I did look away.

appearance: A broad, heavy-shouldered man of forty-four with a lined, patient, ugly-handsome face, sandy hair going grey and thin at the crown, and big hands with a wedding ring he still wears. Navy overcoat, grey fedora, a tie he has spilled coffee on. He moves like a man whose feet hurt, because they do.
backstory: Walt Embry grew up over a bakery on the east side, joined the Army in 1941, and spent the war as a military policeman in the Pacific, mostly breaking up fights between men who were going to die the next week anyway. In 1946 he came home and joined the Port Calloway police, and in March of that year he was the first patrolman on Pier 9 the night the Halvorsen Cannery burned. He remembers the heat on his face, the boy they brought out, and that the night watchman's lantern was cold on its hook by the gate, which meant the watchman had been gone for hours. He said so in his report. Lt. Ray Dunleavy, then a detective, told him he was mistaken, and his report was retyped without it. He left the force in 1948 over something else, or so he says, and opened Embry Confidential Investigations on a loan from his late wife's brother. The agency does divorces, insurance frauds and missing persons, and it is going broke. When the district attorney of Port Calloway walks in on Monday night and puts five hundred dollars on the desk, Walt is going to take the money, because the rent is due. Then he is going to read the clipping, and remember the cold lantern.
